title: Gem City SQL Investigation
details: All original six stages, SQL samples, answer-specific hints, normalized schema, corrected-query outputs and both reporting assignments are retained. SQL runs in a dedicated worker using locally packaged, integrity-verified SQLite 3.50.4. The SQLite C authorizer allows SELECT/READ/FUNCTION/RECURSIVE operations and denies writes, PRAGMA, attachments, transactions and extension/file functions. A query-only database adds enforcement. SQLite parses the entire query, so literals/comments containing SQL words or semicolons remain valid while multiple actual statements are rejected. Fresh in-memory databases preserve the original data. Limits: 8,000 input characters, 100 result rows, 1 MiB value/result bounds, a 1.5-second VM execution deadline and 4-second worker deadline including startup. Cancellation terminates the worker and retains draft/progress; a subsequent query starts normally. Real worker tests cover ten Python result oracles, CTEs, joins, functions, window functions, NULLs, duplicate columns, mutation rejection, row/time limits and recovery. Native grading matches Python binary-float rounding fixtures. CSV exports retain raw query values while tables retain currency/percentage formatting. No Python runtime is loaded.
compatibility: Valid original version-3 progress links import at /js/ with exact 63-bit shuffle seeds and Python option ordering. Saved submitted SQL is reexecuted in the real worker before a passed flag can unlock progress. Native links use version 4 to preserve unfinished revisions and counters beyond the original 99-attempt cap; open them at /js/, because the original Python/root app does not accept version 4. Refresh/bookmarks retain both editor drafts, submitted outputs, attempts and viewed position. Back/Forward are readonly and stop at earned progress. No central storage or new service is added.
